content.content_text: The 79th Cannes Film Festival took place from May 12 to 23, 2026, with South Korea's Park Chan-wook as jury president. Romania's Cristian Mungiu won his second Palme d'Or with Fjord (2026), after 4 Months, 3 Weeks and 2 Days (2007). The directing prize ended in a tie between the duo Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi, for La bola negra (2026), and Paweł Pawlikowski, for Ojczyzna (Fatherland, 2026), and the acting prizes were shared by pairs of actresses and actors. Peter Jackson, Barbra Streisand and John Travolta received honorary Palmes d'Or.

content.content_text: The 78th Cannes Film Festival took place from May 13 to 24, 2025, with Juliette Binoche as jury president. Iran's Jafar Panahi won the Palme d'Or with Un simple accident (It Was Just an Accident, 2025). Brazil left the festival with two awards for O Agente Secreto (The Secret Agent, 2025): Kleber Mendonça Filho won best director and Wagner Moura best actor. Robert De Niro and Denzel Washington received honorary Palmes d'Or.

content.content_text: The 77th Cannes Film Festival took place from May 14 to 25, 2024, with Greta Gerwig as jury president. Anora (2024), by Sean Baker, won the Palme d'Or, and the four actresses of Emilia Pérez (2024) shared the Best Actress award. Sentenced to prison in Iran, Mohammad Rasoulof fled the country to present Les Graines du figuier sauvage (The Seed of the Sacred Fig, 2024), which received a special jury prize. Meryl Streep, Studio Ghibli and George Lucas received honorary Palmes d'Or.

content.content_text: The 76th Cannes Film Festival took place from May 16 to 27, 2023, with Sweden's Ruben Östlund, the previous year's Palme winner, as jury president. With Anatomie d'une chute (Anatomy of a Fall, 2023), Justine Triet became the third woman to win the Palme d'Or, after Jane Campion (1993) and Julia Ducournau (2021). The Zone of Interest (2023), by Jonathan Glazer, took the Grand Prix. The festival opened with Maïwenn's Jeanne du Barry and presented honorary Palmes d'Or to Michael Douglas and Harrison Ford.

content.content_text: The 75th Cannes Film Festival took place from May 17 to 28, 2022, with French actor Vincent Lindon as jury president and actress Virginie Efira as master of ceremonies. Sweden's Ruben Östlund won his second Palme d'Or with the satire Triangle of Sadness (2022), five years after The Square. To celebrate the festival's anniversary, the jury gave a 75th Anniversary Prize to Tori et Lokita (Tori and Lokita, 2022), by the Dardenne brothers, and honorary Palmes d'Or went to Forest Whitaker and Tom Cruise.

content.content_text: The 74th Cannes Film Festival took place from July 6 to 17, 2021, postponed from May due to the COVID-19 pandemic, a year after the 2020 edition was canceled. The jury was presided over by Spike Lee, the first Black person to hold the post, and the opening film was Annette (2021), which earned Leos Carax the directing prize. Titane (2021) gave the Palme d'Or to Julia Ducournau, the second woman to win the award and the first to win it alone (in 1993, Jane Campion shared the Palme with Chen Kaige). At the closing ceremony, Spike Lee mistakenly announced the Palme winner right at the start of the evening.
